intro1
Brightloop SMS — Subscription Management System
Hello everyone! Welcome to Brightloop S M S, a complete subscription management system that we built for this hackathon.
intro2
Plans · Quotations · Subscriptions · Billing · Invoices · Payments · Portal

Businesses that sell recurring services, like software licences or cloud hosting, need to manage plans, quotations, subscriptions, invoices and payments. Brightloop does all of this in one place. Let me show you how it works, step by step.
login
Secure login · bcrypt + httpOnly sessions · 3 roles

We start at the login page. Authentication uses email and password. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, and sessions use secure, http-only cookies. There are three roles: admin, internal staff, and customer. For this demo, I will sign in as the admin, with one click.
dash1
Live KPIs across 5,000 subscriptions & ~30,000 invoices

This is the admin dashboard. At the top, we have the key numbers: active subscriptions, monthly recurring revenue, annual recurring revenue, revenue collected this month, the outstanding amount, and the overdue amount. All of this is calculated live, across five thousand subscriptions and nearly thirty thousand invoices.
dash2
Invoiced vs collected · Subscriptions by status
This chart compares the amount invoiced with the amount actually collected, month by month, for the last twelve months. On the right, we can see how many subscriptions are in each status.
dash3
Overdue invoices · one-click Chase reminder · aging

Below that are the overdue invoices, with the biggest balances first. With one click on Chase, the system emails a payment reminder to the customer. And the aging chart shows how long the money has been pending.
prod1
Products: services & goods with default taxes
Now let's look at the product catalogue. Each product is either a service or goods, with a sales price, a cost price, and default taxes, like G S T at eighteen percent.
prod2
Variant price = sales price + Σ attribute extra price

Products can have variants. The variant price is calculated automatically: the base sales price, plus the extra price of each attribute. For example, the Odoo brand adds five hundred and sixty rupees, and the Enterprise edition adds twelve hundred rupees.
prod3
Configuration is Admin-only · read-only for Internal staff
Attributes and their values are managed here. Only the admin can change the configuration. Internal staff can view it, but for them it is read only.
plans
Recurring plans: period, min quantity, availability, pause / close / renew rules

Recurring plans decide how often we bill: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Each plan also has rules: a minimum quantity, availability dates, and whether the customer may pause, close, or renew. A plan can even auto-close its subscriptions after its end date.
disc
Automatic discounts · date window · usage limit · minimums

Discounts are applied automatically when an invoice is created, but only if the discount is active, within its dates, below its usage limit, and the minimum quantity or purchase is met. Look at this Diwali offer. It has reached its limit of one hundred and fifty uses, so the system has stopped applying it.
tmpl1
Quotation templates
Now, the sales flow. Quotation templates are ready-made bundles of a plan and products. Let's create a quotation from the Starter C R M template.
tmpl2
Plan and lines copied from the template
The plan and the product lines are copied from the template. I just select the customer.
tmpl3
Variant prices auto-filled · minimum quantity checked · validity from template

Prices are picked up from the variant automatically, and quantities are checked against the plan's minimum. Now I click Create quotation. The quotation is valid only for the number of days set in the template. After that, it cannot be confirmed.
sm1
State machine: Draft → Quotation → Confirmed → Active → Closed

Every subscription follows a strict state machine: draft, quotation, confirmed, active, and finally closed. You can see this in the status stepper. Illegal moves are rejected on the server, and every change is recorded in the history. Let me confirm the quotation, and then activate it.
sm2
Plan-aware actions · next-invoice preview with discounts & GST

The subscription is now active. The pause, renew and close buttons appear only if the plan allows them. On the right, we get a preview of the next invoice, with discounts and G S T already calculated. Let me click Bill now.
sm3
Invoice generated · full status history
The first invoice has been generated, and the complete status history is shown here: who did what, and when.
bill1
Billing engine: one invoice per due period · catch-up · batches of 100

Next, the billing engine, which is the heart of the system. When we run billing, it picks every active subscription that is due, and creates one invoice for each billing period. If a subscription has missed several periods, it gets one invoice for every missed period. Nothing is skipped. It works in batches of one hundred.
bill2
Run 1: invoices created + ended plans auto-closed
The first run created new invoices, and also automatically closed the subscriptions whose plan had ended. Now, watch carefully. I will run billing again.
bill3
Run 2: 0 created — idempotent, never billed twice

Zero invoices created. The billing run is idempotent. A unique key on the subscription and the billing period guarantees that a customer is never billed twice for the same period, even if billing runs again by mistake.
bill4
Run history · manual, daily scheduler, or secure cron endpoint
Every run is saved in the history. Billing can be started manually, by a daily scheduler, or from a secure cron endpoint.
inv1
Discounts as visible lines · tax per line after discount
Now let's open a draft invoice. Each discount appears as its own line on the invoice, and tax is calculated on each line after the discount. Let me confirm this invoice.
inv2
Payments only on confirmed invoices · overpayment blocked
Payments can be recorded only on confirmed invoices. If I try to enter more than the amount due, the system blocks the overpayment.
inv3
Partial payment · amounts update atomically
Partial payments are allowed. I will record one thousand rupees. The amount paid and the amount due are updated together, in a single transaction.
inv4
Fully paid → PAID automatically · PDF & email built in

Now I pay the remaining balance. As soon as the amount due becomes zero, the invoice is marked as paid, automatically. Invoices can also be printed, downloaded as a P D F, and emailed to the customer.
list1
Server-side pagination, sorting & filters · pages load < 1s

All the lists are built for scale. There are five thousand subscriptions here, but the server sends only twenty five rows at a time, with sorting and filtering done on the server. That is why every page loads in under one second.
rep1
Reports with filters and one-click CSV export
The reports page summarises revenue, payments, overdue invoices, and active subscriptions. We can filter by date range, customer and plan, and export everything to C S V with one click.
portal1
Customer portal
Finally, let's see it from the customer's side. I will log out, and sign in to the customer portal.
portal2
Customers see only their own data — enforced on the server
The customer sees only their own subscriptions, invoices and payments. This is enforced on the server for every single query, so one customer can never see another customer's data.
portal3
Accept quotations
From here, the customer can accept a quotation sent by our team,
portal4
Pause or cancel — only if the plan allows
pause or cancel a subscription, but only if their plan allows it,
portal5
Download invoices · pay online
and download their invoices, or pay them online.
rbac
Role-based access control
And if a customer tries to open the admin dashboard, role based access control sends them straight back to their portal.
outro
Next.js 14 · TypeScript · Zod · RBAC · idempotent billing · 40 unit tests

So, that is Brightloop S M S. Built with Next.js fourteen and TypeScript, with Zod validation on every input, role based access control, an idempotent billing engine, and forty unit tests covering the key business rules. Thank you for watching!
